evidence: New resume created with blank contact fields (empty full-name, email, phone, location), blank summary (0/500), empty experience list, empty education list, and "No skills added yet" message. Editing begins immediately.
Contact fields, summary text, both experience entries, education entry, and both skills all appeared in preview immediately after entry without saving/refresh.

Edited contact details and summary; added 2 experience entries, reordered them (move-up/move-down), edited position field, added a 3rd and removed it; added education entry; added 2 skills, changed one's level to Expert, removed the other. All changes reflected correctly.

Dates use month input (type=month) and render consistently as 'Mon YYYY' in preview for both experience and education (e.g. 'Jan 2020', 'Sep 2013'). Checking 'I currently work here' cleared the end-date value and disabled the end-date field; preview showed 'Jan 2020 - Present'.

issue: No validation for invalid experience date ranges
actual: Set start=2020-01, end=2019-01 (end before start): no error message appeared anywhere in the UI, and the preview happily rendered 'Jan 2020 - Jan 2019' with no rejection or feedback. Then changed end date to a future value 2030-01: the editor input accepted and displayed '2030-01', but the preview silently kept showing the stale 'Jan 2019' value instead of updating or showing an error - i.e. inconsistent state with no clear validation feedback in either case.

evidence: Switched between Modern, Classic, and Minimal templates. Preview visibly re-styled each time (uppercase headings in Classic/Minimal, different separators) while all contact, summary, experience, education, and skills content remained intact.

issue: Customized section heading not rendered in Minimal style
actual: Renamed the Summary section heading to 'About Me' via Sections tab. It correctly appeared as 'About Me' in Modern and 'ABOUT ME' in Classic style, but the Minimal template renders the summary text as a plain paragraph with no heading element at all - the customized (or any) section title is completely missing from the Minimal preview for that visible section.

evidence: Moved Education section above Experience via move-up control; preview order updated accordingly (Education now precedes Work Experience). Toggled Skills section visibility off; preview no longer shows the Skills section/heading.

Reordered sections (Education before Experience) and hid Skills section; layout updated immediately in preview and remained intact after switching tabs and after navigating to dashboard and back into the resume.

After editing contact/summary/experience/education/skills/sections/template, navigated back to dashboard - card showed 'Updated Aug 26, 2026' (today) confirming dashboard reflects the update. Reopened resume and all edits were retained.
Contact details, summary, experience entries, education entry, and skills all remained present after switching editor tabs, going to dashboard, and reopening the resume.

Clicked 'Hide Preview' - toggle changed to 'Show Preview' and preview content was no longer accessible/rendered. Clicked 'Show Preview' - preview reappeared with all contact/summary/education/experience content intact and the Classic template style preserved. Editor form fields also remained populated throughout.

issue: No validation feedback shown when rejecting empty/whitespace title
actual: Editing the title field and submitting whitespace-only text ('   ') correctly reverted to the prior title 'Untitled Resume' (title itself preserved as required), but no error/toast/inline validation message was shown to the user anywhere on the page (Notifications region remained empty) to explain why the change was rejected.

evidence: Renamed resume title from 'Untitled Resume' to 'Backend Engineer Resume'; editor title updated immediately, and dashboard card also shows 'Backend Engineer Resume' after navigating back.

Duplicated 'Backend Engineer Resume' via card menu -> Duplicate, producing 'Backend Engineer Resume (Copy)'. Renamed the copy to 'Backend Engineer Resume - Startup App' via Rename dialog. Edited the copy's full name to 'Alex Tester Copy'; original resume's full name remained 'Alex Tester' unaffected.

Dashboard now holds 5 distinct resumes in the same session: original 3 sample resumes, 'Backend Engineer Resume' (newly created), and 'Backend Engineer Resume - Startup App' (its duplicate/renamed variant) - each independently editable.

After duplicating, edited copy's full-name to 'Alex Tester Copy' - original stayed 'Alex Tester'. Then edited original's location to 'Boston, MA' - copy's location remained 'New York, NY'. Changes in either direction did not propagate to the other.

Searching 'backend' (lowercase) matched 'Backend Engineer Resume' and 'Backend Engineer Resume - Startup App' (case-insensitive). Clearing search restored all 5 resumes. Sorting 'Oldest First' ordered resumes Jan 2024 -> Aug 2026; switching to 'Newest First' reversed to Aug 2026 -> Jan 2024.

issue: Date filtering feature is missing entirely
actual: The dashboard only provides a title search box and a sort-by-date dropdown (Newest/Oldest/Title A-Z/Title Z-A). There is no UI control anywhere (including hidden elements) to filter resumes by an exact creation date or a date range. Users cannot narrow resumes by creation date at all.

issue: No persistence across reload - all session changes are lost
actual: Created a new resume ('Backend Engineer Resume'), edited its content, duplicated it, renamed the duplicate to 'Backend Engineer Resume - Startup App', edited the duplicate, then deleted the original. After reloading the page (http://localhost:6005/), the dashboard reverted to only the original 3 seed resumes (Product Designer, Marketing Manager, Software Engineer) - the created/duplicated/renamed resume was gone entirely, and none of the session's create/edit/duplicate/rename/delete actions survived. localStorage and sessionStorage are both empty, confirming the app keeps all resume data only in in-memory state with no persistence.

evidence: For the Modern style, all visible sections with content (contact, summary, 10 experience entries, education, skills) rendered in the preview with full, untruncated text (verified a 245-char description rendered in full, no CSS clipping/ellipsis). When content volume was increased (10 experience entries with long descriptions) causing total page height (4682px) to exceed a constrained 500px viewport, the page became scrollable (documentElement scrollHeight 4682 vs clientHeight 500) allowing the user to scroll down and reach all resume content - nothing was cut off or hidden.
